questions.question: Residents of a town were surveyed to determine whether they are satisfied with the concession stand at the local park. A random sample of 200 residents was selected. All 200 responded, and 87% said they are satisfied. Based on this information, which of the following statements must be true? I. Of all the town residents, 87% would say they are satisfied with the concession stand at the local park. Il. If another random sample of 200 residents were surveyed, 87% would say they are satisfied.
options: Neither
I only
Il only
I and Il

questions.question: For a baobab tree habitat in South Africa, a scientist randomly selected 50 baobab trees that were 17 years old and randomly assigned them to two groups. Each group was subjected to a different watering pattern for 2 consecutive years to observe whether the watering pattern affects the trees' growth rate. Based on the design of the study, what is the largest group to which these results can be applied?
options: All the 50 baobab trees that were selected in this habitat
All the baobab trees that were 19 years old in this habitat
All the baobab trees that were 17 years old in South Africa
All the baobab trees that were 17 years old in this habitat

questions.question: A psychologist designed and conducted a study to determine whether playing a certain educational game increases middle school students' accuracy in adding fractions. For the study, the psychologist chose a random sample of 35 students from all of the students at one of the middle schools in a large city. The psychologist found that students who played the game showed significant improvement in accuracy when adding fractions. What is the largest group to which the results of the study can be generalized?
options: The 35 students in the sample
All students at the school
All middle school students in the city
All students in the city

questions.question: The members of a city council wanted to assess the opinions of all city residents about converting an open field into a dog park. The council surveyed a sample of 500 city residents who own dogs. The survey showed that the majority of those sampled were in favor of the dog park. Which of the following is true about the city council's survey?
options: It shows that the majority of city residents are in favor of the dog park.
The survey sample should have included more residents who are dog owners.
The survey sample should have consisted entirely of residents who do not own dogs.
The survey sample is biased because it is not representative of all city residents.

questions.question: Near the end of a US cable news show, the host invited viewers to respond to a poll on the show's website that asked, "Do you support the new federal policy discussed during the show?" At the end of the show, the host reported that 28% responded "Yes," and 70% responded "No." Which of the following best explains why the results are unlikely to represent the sentiments of the population of the United States?
options: The percentages do not add up to 100%, so any possible conclusions from the poll are invalid.
Those who responded to the poll were not a random sample of the population of the United States.
There were not 50% "Yes" responses and 50% "No" responses.
The show did not allow viewers enough time to respond to the poll.

questions.question: Researchers randomly sample 100 city voters but do not assign any treatment. What does the random sampling primarily support?
options: Establishing a causal effect of a treatment
Guaranteeing that every response is truthful
Eliminating all sampling variability
Generalizing the sample results to the population of city voters
questions.explanation: D is correct. Random sampling supports representativeness and population generalization.
questions.teachingTopic: 随机抽样、随机分组与代表性

questions.question: Researchers recruit 110 volunteers and randomly assign them to two exercise plans. What does the random assignment primarily support?
options: Comparing the methods in a way that can support a causal conclusion for the participants
Generalizing automatically to every student
Guaranteeing identical outcomes
Removing the need for a control group
questions.explanation: A is correct. Random assignment balances other factors between treatment groups and supports causal inference.
questions.teachingTopic: 随机抽样、随机分组与代表性

questions.question: Researchers take a random sample of 120 county households and then randomly assign the sampled participants to two reminder messages. What can the design potentially support?
options: Neither generalization nor causal comparison
Both population generalization and a causal comparison
Only a description of volunteers
A conclusion with no uncertainty
questions.explanation: B is correct. Random sampling supports generalization, and random assignment supports causation.
questions.teachingTopic: 随机抽样、随机分组与代表性
